import pandas as pd

# File paths for all source CSV files
source_files = [
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length5_66/training_0.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length5_66/training_1.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length5_66/training_2.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length5_66/training_3.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length5_66/training_4.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length5_66/training_5.csv"
]

# Target schema columns and their types (for reference and enforcement)
target_columns = [
    'S/N',
    'Building/Project Name',
    'Street Name',
    'Postal District',
    'Type',
    'No. of Bedroom(for Non-Landed Only)',
    'Monthly Gross Rent($)',
    'Floor Area (sq ft)',
    'Lease Commencement Date'
]

# Load all source dataframes into a list
dfs = []
for file in source_files:
    # index_col=0 to ignore the first numerical index column as per Hint 24
    df = pd.read_csv(file, index_col=0)
    dfs.append(df)

# All source tables have exactly the same schema as the target schema (column names and order),
# so we can safely concatenate (union) all source dataframes.
combined_df = pd.concat(dfs, ignore_index=True)

# Data type and formatting adjustments to match target schema and examples:

# 1. 'S/N': convert to string (some source have float, target expects string)
combined_df['S/N'] = combined_df['S/N'].astype(str).str.replace('.0$', '', regex=True)

# 2. 'Building/Project Name': string, strip whitespace
combined_df['Building/Project Name'] = combined_df['Building/Project Name'].astype(str).str.strip()

# 3. 'Street Name': string, uppercase and strip whitespace to match target examples style
combined_df['Street Name'] = combined_df['Street Name'].astype(str).str.strip().str.upper()

# 4. 'Postal District': float, ensure numeric, coerce errors to NaN
combined_df['Postal District'] = pd.to_numeric(combined_df['Postal District'], errors='coerce')

# 5. 'Type': string, strip whitespace
combined_df['Type'] = combined_df['Type'].astype(str).str.strip()

# 6. 'No. of Bedroom(for Non-Landed Only)': string in target, source has float or 'na*'
#    Convert numeric to string without trailing '.0', keep 'na*' as is, fill NaN with 'na*'
def convert_bedroom(val):
    if pd.isna(val):
        return 'na*'
    if isinstance(val, str):
        val_strip = val.strip()
        if val_strip.lower() == 'na*':
            return 'na*'
        try:
            f = float(val_strip)
            if f.is_integer():
                return str(int(f))
            else:
                return str(f)
        except:
            return val_strip
    if isinstance(val, (int, float)):
        if pd.isna(val):
            return 'na*'
        if float(val).is_integer():
            return str(int(val))
        else:
            return str(val)
    return str(val)

combined_df['No. of Bedroom(for Non-Landed Only)'] = combined_df['No. of Bedroom(for Non-Landed Only)'].apply(convert_bedroom)

# 7. 'Monthly Gross Rent($)': float, ensure numeric, coerce errors to NaN
combined_df['Monthly Gross Rent($)'] = pd.to_numeric(combined_df['Monthly Gross Rent($)'], errors='coerce')

# 8. 'Floor Area (sq ft)': string, strip whitespace
combined_df['Floor Area (sq ft)'] = combined_df['Floor Area (sq ft)'].astype(str).str.strip()

# 9. 'Lease Commencement Date': string, strip whitespace
combined_df['Lease Commencement Date'] = combined_df['Lease Commencement Date'].astype(str).str.strip()

# Reorder columns to exactly match target schema (just in case)
combined_df = combined_df[target_columns]

# Save the combined and transformed dataframe to the target CSV file
combined_df.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length5_66/target_multisource_cot.csv", index=False)

import pandas as pd

# Read all source CSV files with index_col=0 to ignore the first numerical index column
df0 = pd.read_csv('autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length5_66/training_0.csv', index_col=0)
df1 = pd.read_csv('autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length5_66/training_1.csv', index_col=0)
df2 = pd.read_csv('autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length5_66/training_2.csv', index_col=0)
df3 = pd.read_csv('autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length5_66/training_3.csv', index_col=0)
df4 = pd.read_csv('autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length5_66/training_4.csv', index_col=0)
df5 = pd.read_csv('autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length5_66/training_5.csv', index_col=0)

# All source tables have the same schema and represent partitions of the same data.
# The target table has the same schema as sources.
# Therefore, UNION all source tables to get the full dataset.

df_all = pd.concat([df0, df1, df2, df3, df4, df5], ignore_index=True)

# According to the target schema and examples:
# - 'S/N' is string in target, convert accordingly
# - 'Building/Project Name' string
# - 'Street Name' string
# - 'Postal District' float
# - 'Type' string
# - 'No. of Bedroom(for Non-Landed Only)' string in target, convert from float or na* to string
# - 'Monthly Gross Rent($)' float
# - 'Floor Area (sq ft)' string
# - 'Lease Commencement Date' string

# Convert 'S/N' to string (some are float in source)
df_all['S/N'] = df_all['S/N'].astype(str)

# Convert 'Building/Project Name' and 'Street Name' and 'Type' to string (should already be)
df_all['Building/Project Name'] = df_all['Building/Project Name'].astype(str)
df_all['Street Name'] = df_all['Street Name'].astype(str)
df_all['Type'] = df_all['Type'].astype(str)

# 'Postal District' to float (some may be int or float)
df_all['Postal District'] = pd.to_numeric(df_all['Postal District'], errors='coerce')

# 'No. of Bedroom(for Non-Landed Only)' convert to string, handle 'na*' or missing values
df_all['No. of Bedroom(for Non-Landed Only)'] = df_all['No. of Bedroom(for Non-Landed Only)'].astype(str)

# 'Monthly Gross Rent($)' to float
df_all['Monthly Gross Rent($)'] = pd.to_numeric(df_all['Monthly Gross Rent($)'], errors='coerce')

# 'Floor Area (sq ft)' string
df_all['Floor Area (sq ft)'] = df_all['Floor Area (sq ft)'].astype(str)

# 'Lease Commencement Date' string
df_all['Lease Commencement Date'] = df_all['Lease Commencement Date'].astype(str)

# Remove duplicates if any (based on all columns)
df_all = df_all.drop_duplicates()

# The target examples have about 194223 tuples, so no group by aggregation is needed.
# But to ensure uniqueness on 'S/N' (which is unique in target), group by 'S/N' and take first row.
# This also ensures no duplicates on primary key.

df_final = df_all.groupby('S/N', as_index=False).first()

# Write to target CSV
df_final.to_csv('autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length5_66/target_multisource_critique_history.csv', index=False)
